message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Series | Title | Year | Notes |
|--------|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter** | *Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone* (UK) / *Sorcerer’s Stone* (US) | 1997 | First book in the series; introduces Harry, Hogwarts, and the wizarding world. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets* | 1998 | Second book; explores the mystery of the Chamber and the basilisk. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban* | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire* | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix* | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s interference. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince* | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s past and the Horcruxes. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows* | 2007 | Seventh book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **Fantastic Beasts** | *Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them* | 2001 | Companion book to the Harry Potter films; Rowling’s guide to magical creatures. |
| | *Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald* | 2018 | First novel in the Fantastic Beasts film series. |
| | *Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore* | 2022 | Second novel in the Fantastic Beasts film series. |
| **Other Works** | *The Casual Vacancy* | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a dark comedy about a small town’s political drama. |
| | *The Cuckoo’s Calling* (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | First book in the Cormoran Strike detective series. |
| | *The Silkworm* (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| | *Career of Evil* (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| | *Lethal White* (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| | *The Ickabog* | 2020 | A children’s fairy‑tale book released as a free online story. |

These titles span Rowling’s most famous series, her ventures into adult fiction, and her work under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith. They have all enjoyed significant commercial success and critical acclaim.
